detail:
The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) describes rhinitis, which affects the nose, and rhinosinusitis among the allergic diseases with very high prevalence in the United States and around the world. NIAID states that the development, history, genetics, diagnosis, management, and prevention of these conditions are important scientific research areas for the institute, pursued through investigator-initiated projects in basic research and clinical trials.

Research structures described by NIAID include the Asthma and Allergic Diseases Cooperative Research Centers, which conduct integrated clinical and translational research on the immune mechanisms of asthma, rhinitis, and related conditions, and laboratory work on how environmental allergens trigger and sustain allergic inflammation through innate and adaptive immune responses. NIAID also lists new forms of allergen immunotherapy for allergic rhinitis among its high-priority research topics, aimed at improved efficacy, safety, and faster induction of lasting tolerance. The sources present these directions as ongoing research programs rather than established new treatments.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about allergic rhinitis research and clinical trials.
sourceName: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases
summary: NIAID presents rhinitis as a major allergic disease research area, with cooperative research centers studying immune mechanisms of rhinitis and related conditions and high-priority work on new forms of allergen immunotherapy.
takeaways: niaid studies rhinitis genetics, diagnosis, and prevention
cooperative centers research immune mechanisms of rhinitis
new allergen immunotherapy forms are a research priority
title: Allergic rhinitis: research into immune mechanisms and immunotherapy
